title: Compute and Classify Under the New Policy
skill: Deriving and applying rules in one pass
scenario: It is 6:30 AM. At Easy tier the percent moves were handed to you. Not today: you have raw actuals, raw prior-day values, and the freshly versioned 1.1.0 policy (routine 6, escalation 14). Compute each hub's move, round it the way the desk rounds, and classify it.
input:
Threshold Policy v1.1.0 (day-over-day percent move, size of the move regardless of direction):
- Under 6 percent: normal.
- 6 percent or more, but under 14: routine.
- 14 percent or more: escalate.

Raw values (actual vs prior day):
ERCOT: actual 204, prior day 176
SPP: actual 98.5, prior day 97
WAUE: actual 63, prior day 59

Desk rounding rule: pctMove = (actual - priorDay) / priorDay * 100, rounded to 1 decimal place.
instructions: Compute each hub's pctMove with the desk formula and round to 1 decimal.
Classify each hub against the 1.1.0 bands (6 and 14), using the size of the move.
Return a JSON array with one object per hub, then validate.
copilotPrompt: For each hub compute pctMove = (actual - priorDay) / priorDay * 100 rounded to 1 decimal, then classify with bands: under 6 normal, 6 to under 14 routine, 14 or more escalate. ERCOT 204/176, SPP 98.5/97, WAUE 63/59. Return a JSON array of { hub, pctMove, status }.
successMessage: Risk record computed and classified under policy 1.1.0 - the same workflow, correctly obeying a changed rule.

intro.heading: Before you build: the formula is part of the rule

sections.title: Rounding is a governed choice
sections.body: 15.909 and 15.9 and 16 are three different claims. The desk rounds to 1 decimal - not because it is right in the abstract, but because every step agreeing on one rounding rule is what keeps records comparable.

sections.title: New version, new behavior
sections.body: Under 1.0.0, WAUE's 6.8 percent move would have been routine and ERCOT's 15.9 would still escalate - but a 13 percent day would have flipped. You are watching a policy change propagate through unchanged workflow logic. That separation is the whole point of config-as-rules.

sections.title: Classify on size, report with sign
sections.body: Same discipline as Easy tier: the bands care about magnitude, the record keeps direction. A rule you learned once now holds under harder arithmetic.

takeaway.heading: Risk classified under the changed rule
points: You derived the percent moves yourself, with the desk's rounding rule as part of the computation contract.
You applied version 1.1.0's bands - and saw how a policy change alters outcomes without any workflow logic changing.
WAUE was excluded from variance (no forecast) but classified here (day-over-day data exists) - two steps with different data requirements, both honest.
ERCOT escalates again; the routing tier ahead will handle it with a complication.
The workflow can now derive and classify risk under whichever policy version is in force.
